Controlling Stylized Anime Facial Shadows Prototype demo for M.S. proposal · Jingwen Liu (HUST)

To avoid bumpy shading from raw 3D face normals, anime character shaders rely on painted shadow masks. This prototype lets you adjust when the nose shadow separates from the cheek, and compares a single merged layer against separated nose and cheek layers.

1. Light direction & split control 2. Single-layer ceiling vs. 2-layer & 19-key 3. Transfer to a second head

1. Controlling the nose–cheek split across light azimuth and elevation

At 70°, only the right portrait opens a lit gap between nose and cheek. Drag the middle red knot above 70° to close it, or switch elevations across the 5×3 keys on Sendagaya_Shino.vrm.

2. Single-layer ceiling: 1-layer vs. 2-layer and a 19-key reference

Fixed elevation (ψ = 0°). The first two panels use phase-warped 5-key SDFs with 2 outer cheek pins (merged vs. pre-split procedural nose and cheek layers), while the third uses 19 threshold keys (every 10°). Scrub θ across 68° to compare.

Contour error across 12 test angles (640 px) θ = 70.0°
Click anywhere on the plot to jump θ. Same data as proposal Fig. 1b.
Single-layer limit: In the merged 45° key, the cheek absorbs the nose shadow's inner edge, so single-layer interpolation rounds the emerging nose tip near 68°. Even with two outer cheek pins, contour error reaches ~40 px at 70°, and adding a third pin inside [45°, 90°] worsened mean error (18.2 px vs. 15.7 px).
Next step: At 70°, the two-layer version preserves the sharp nose tip. Recovering those hidden inner edges from hand-drawn merged keyframes, along with editable sharp/soft joins and head-turn adaptation, is the focus of my M.S. plan.

3. Transferring to a second character head without painting new masks

12 matching landmarks warp Shino's five key masks, split anchor, and outer timing pins onto KayKit Mage.glb via a thin-plate spline (TPS).

Blender 3.6 renders at θ = 70° (target split 68°)

Hover any landmark dot to inspect how Shino's face UV maps onto the Mage.

Raw N·L leaves Mage's flatter face mostly dark, direct UV copy lands on the mouth, and TPS + threshold still splits late.

CC0 3D heads: Sendagaya_Shino.vrm (VRoid Project) and KayKit Mage.glb (Kay Lousberg), rendered in Blender 3.6. Prototype demo accompanying Jingwen Liu's M.S. research proposal.
